MMSpower

MMSpower

Sample size, power and analysis for malaria molecular surveillance studies, allowing for imperfect diagnostic tests and sampling clustered across sites.

Get started Tutorials Reference

Why MMSpower

Malaria programmes increasingly use molecular surveillance, for example of drug-resistance markers or pfhrp2/3 deletions, to make decisions. These surveys are often clustered across sites, rely on imperfect assays, and need to be tailored to local constraints. MMSpower provides straightforward functions for designing a study and analysing its results, with a focus on malaria molecular surveillance (MMS) applications.

A first example

How many samples are needed to estimate a prevalence of around 30% to within ±5 percentage points, sampling 10 people per site with an ICC of 0.05?

library(MMSpower)

design_precision(prevalence = 0.3, moe = 0.05, n_per_site = 10, icc = 0.05)
#> $n
#> [1] 500
#>
#> $n_sites
#> [1] 50
#>
#> $n_per_site
#> [1] 10
#>
#> $deff
#> [1] 1.45
#>
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 341
#>
#> $moe
#> [1] 0.04965355

50 sites of 10 people, giving a margin of error just under the 5-point target. Without clustering, 341 people would be enough; the design effect of 1.45 accounts for people at the same site resembling each other.

The tutorials take each type of study from design through to analysis, starting with estimating prevalence.
